# Engineering With Bandarage

> Sameera Bandarage, certified engineer: free, in-depth tutorials on data engineering, Snowflake, dbt, Airflow, SQL Server data warehousing, Power BI, statistics, AI systems and power electronics, each built on a working lab.

Free, in-depth engineering tutorials by Sameera Bandarage. Every example, number and screenshot comes from a working lab (SQL Server, Snowflake, dbt, Airflow, Power BI) run on an AWS virtual machine.
Contact: LinkedIn, https://www.linkedin.com/in/sameeradatabee/

## AI & AI Systems Engineering

- [AI & AI Systems Engineering track](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/ai/): The AI and AI Systems Engineering track: building, evaluating and operating AI systems on top of a governed data platform.
- [AI Systems Engineering: From Data Platform to Production AI](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/ai/ai-systems-engineering/): AI Systems Engineering: building, evaluating and operating production AI systems on a governed data platform.
  - [The Big Picture](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/ai/ai-systems-engineering/01-big-picture): What an AI system is beyond the model: data, retrieval, tools, evaluation, guardrails and operations, how it differs from a data pipeline, and where it sits on the data platform built in the other tracks.

## AI for Logistics and Transportation

- [AI for Logistics and Transportation track](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/ai-logistics/): The AI for Logistics and Transportation track: AI use cases across planning, fleet, warehouse and freight operations, and a practical guide to transforming a logistics company around data and AI.
- [AI Use Cases for Logistics and Transportation: The Transformation Playbook](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/ai-logistics/playbook/): A practical guide to AI in logistics and transportation: use cases across planning, fleet, warehouse and freight operations, and how to transform a logistics company around data and AI, built on Iansiti and Lakhani's Competing in the Age of AI and current industry research.
  - [Why AI Changes Logistics](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/ai-logistics/playbook/01-why-ai-changes-logistics): Why AI changes the logistics firm itself: business model versus operating model, digital scale, scope and learning, moving people off the critical path, and lessons from Amazon, Ocado and UPS.
  - [The Logistics AI Factory](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/ai-logistics/playbook/02-logistics-ai-factory): The AI factory applied to logistics: the data pipeline and datafication of physical operations, supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning, generative AI and agents, experimentation without A/B tests, and the platform underneath.
  - [Rearchitecting the Logistics Firm](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/ai-logistics/playbook/03-rearchitecting-the-firm): Why AI needs a new operating architecture in logistics: the mirroring hypothesis, TMS, WMS and ERP silos, the Bezos API mandate, a data platform with product teams, and the new role of managers.
  - [Planning, Forecasting and Visibility](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/ai-logistics/playbook/04-planning-forecasting): AI use cases in logistics planning: demand and volume forecasting, capacity and labour planning, network design, inventory positioning, predictive ETA, disruption sensing and control towers.
  - [Transportation and Fleet](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/ai-logistics/playbook/05-transport-fleet): AI use cases for transport and fleet operations: route optimisation, dynamic dispatch, load building and empty-mile reduction, predictive maintenance, fuel and emissions, driver safety and coaching, and autonomous vehicles.
  - [Warehouse and Fulfilment](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/ai-logistics/playbook/06-warehouse-fulfilment): AI use cases in the warehouse and distribution centre: slotting, pick paths and batching, labour planning, robotics orchestration, computer vision for inventory and quality, and lessons from Amazon, Ocado, DHL and Maersk.
  - [Freight, Commercial and Back Office](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/ai-logistics/playbook/07-freight-commercial-backoffice): AI use cases in freight commercial and back-office work: dynamic pricing and instant quotes, email-to-order automation, carrier procurement, customs and trade documents, freight audit, claims, customer service and AI agents, with C.H. Robinson and DHL examples.
  - [Choosing the Use-Case Portfolio](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/ai-logistics/playbook/08-portfolio-strategy): How to score, sequence and fund AI use cases in a logistics company, and how to apply strategic network analysis: learning and network effects, clustering, multihoming, disintermediation and network bridging.
  - [The Transformation Roadmap](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/ai-logistics/playbook/09-transformation-roadmap): The AI transformation roadmap for a logistics company: four maturity stages from siloed data to AI factory, the book's five principles, the operating model and roles, KPIs, a 12-month plan, and lessons from Microsoft, Fidelity and GE.
  - [Governance, Risk and Leadership](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/ai-logistics/playbook/10-governance-leadership): Governing AI in logistics: algorithmic bias in driver and worker systems, safety, cybersecurity and hijacking, driver data and privacy, controls for AI agents, regulation such as the EU AI Act, workforce transition and the leadership mandate.

## Data Architecture Design

- [Data Architecture Design track](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/architecture/): The Data Architecture Design track: reference architectures and deployment designs for data platforms, drawn as full-size diagrams.
- [dbt + Airflow + Snowflake Architecture](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/architecture/dbt-airflow-snowflake/): A modern ELT design with dbt, Airflow and Snowflake: the logical reference architecture and two production deployments, on Kubernetes (EKS) and on Linux VMs.
  - [dbt + Airflow + Snowflake](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/architecture/dbt-airflow-snowflake/01-reference-architecture): A reference ELT architecture: sources and ingestion into Snowflake RAW, dbt transforming staging, intermediate and marts inside Snowflake, Airflow orchestrating the run, and BI, ML, reverse ETL and data sharing as consumers.
  - [Deployment on Kubernetes (EKS)](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/architecture/dbt-airflow-snowflake/02-deployment-kubernetes): A production deployment on AWS: Airflow 3 on EKS with the KubernetesExecutor, one image with Airflow, dbt and Cosmos, RDS, Secrets Manager, S3, PrivateLink to Snowflake, and GitHub Actions with Helm.
  - [Deployment on Linux VMs](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/architecture/dbt-airflow-snowflake/03-deployment-linux-vms): Airflow and dbt on Linux VMs without containers: virtualenvs under systemd, CeleryExecutor workers, Ansible releases over SSH, ports and firewall rules, and sizing options.

## Business Intelligence

- [Business Intelligence track](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/bi/): The Business Intelligence track: semantic models, measures and the engineering practices that make reports trustworthy.
- [Power BI Semantic Modelling: From Warehouse Tables to Trusted Measures](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/bi/powerbi-modelling/): Build a Power BI semantic model on AdventureWorksDW2022: star schema on SQL source queries, a 4-4-5 fiscal calendar, a layered P&L measure table, currency and security patterns, the model as code in git, and generated measure documentation.
  - [The Big Picture](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/bi/powerbi-modelling/01-big-picture): Where a Power BI semantic model sits between the warehouse and the reports, the seven rules of the approach, and the Adventure Works P&L built from AdventureWorksDW2022 that every chapter uses.
  - [A Star Schema for Power BI](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/bi/powerbi-modelling/02-star-schema): Grain, conformed dimensions, many-to-one single-direction relationships, a 4-4-5 fiscal calendar inside the Date table and disconnected helper tables, designed on AdventureWorksDW2022.
  - [Getting Data In](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/bi/powerbi-modelling/03-getting-data-in): SQL source queries as the contract, a thin Power Query layer with parameters and native queries that fold, import mode, fiscal-year partitions, and the traps found in the AdventureWorksDW2022 source.
  - [The Fiscal Calendar & Time Intelligence](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/bi/powerbi-modelling/04-fiscal-calendar): A 4-4-5 fiscal calendar with 52 and 53-week years derived in SQL, last year by fiscal week ID with TREATAS, a calculation group for comparisons and a period-to-date selector.
  - [Measure Architecture](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/bi/powerbi-modelling/05-measure-architecture): One measure table, base → line → derived → analysis layers, numbered P&L lines, display folders, format strings, descriptions and the anti-patterns to avoid, from the AdventureWorksPL model.
  - [Advanced Patterns](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/bi/powerbi-modelling/06-advanced-patterns): Local-currency conversion row by row and row-level security by sales territory, all on AdventureWorksDW2022.
  - [The Model as Code](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/bi/powerbi-modelling/07-model-as-code): Power BI projects (PBIP) with the model in TMDL and the report in PBIR, what the AdventureWorksPL definition files contain, git and pull-request reviews, Best Practice Analyzer and deployment.
  - [Reverse-Engineering & Documenting a Model](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/bi/powerbi-modelling/08-reverse-engineering): Load a Power BI model's TMDL definition, build the measure dependency graph, trace every measure to the warehouse columns it reads and generate a page per measure, with a PowerShell script run on AdventureWorksPL.
  - [Testing & Performance](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/bi/powerbi-modelling/09-testing-performance): Reconcile every P&L line with SQL by fiscal period and territory, test the currency, last-year and security patterns, measure performance with a cold cache, and a go-live checklist, with real results from AdventureWorksPL.
  - [DAX Pattern Cheat Sheet](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/bi/powerbi-modelling/appendix-a-dax-patterns): Every DAX pattern from the Power BI Semantic Modelling tutorial on one page, as used in the AdventureWorksPL model.

## Data Warehousing

- [Data Warehousing track](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/datawarehousing/): The Data Warehousing track: building a real data warehouse end to end on SQL Server 2022, orchestrated by Apache Airflow.
- [End-to-End Data Warehouse on Linux + Docker: SQL Server 2022 + Airflow](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/datawarehousing/sqlserver-airflow/): Build the SBEcoLTDDW data warehouse end to end on SQL Server 2022: source profiling, staging, SCD2 dimensions, incremental facts, columnstore, indexed views, Resource Governor, data quality and Airflow orchestration.
  - [The Big Picture](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/datawarehousing/sqlserver-airflow/01-big-picture): The Linux + Docker infrastructure and deployment of the SBEcoLTDDW lab, what a data warehouse is for, the layers of SBEcoLTDDW, ETL vs ELT, and the whole SQL Server + Airflow pipeline on one diagram.
  - [The Lab](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/datawarehousing/sqlserver-airflow/02-the-lab): The SBEcoLTDDW lab: one Ubuntu VM in AWS running SQL Server 2022 and Airflow 2.7 in Docker, the folder layout, the connections and how to rebuild everything.
  - [Dimensional Modelling](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/datawarehousing/sqlserver-airflow/03-dimensional-model): Grain, facts, dimensions, surrogate and smart keys, unknown members, degenerate dimensions and the SBEcoLTDDW star schema on SQL Server 2022.
  - [The Source System](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/datawarehousing/sqlserver-airflow/04-source-system): Profiling AdventureWorks2022 before building the warehouse: row counts, scope, keys, change columns, and the source-to-target mapping for SBEcoLTDDW.
  - [Staging & Extraction](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/datawarehousing/sqlserver-airflow/05-staging-extraction): Full and incremental extracts into a staging schema, a watermark that only advances after a successful run, staging checks and per-step audit logging.
  - [Loading Dimensions](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/datawarehousing/sqlserver-airflow/06-loading-dimensions): A generated date dimension and the customer dimension as SCD Type 1 + Type 2 with a SHA-256 row hash, effective dating from the source and an unknown member.
  - [Loading Facts](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/datawarehousing/sqlserver-airflow/07-loading-facts): Loading Fact.Orders on SQL Server for Linux: scope filters, smart date keys, point-in-time SCD2 lookups, unknown members and an idempotent MERGE.
  - [Indexed Views & Columnstore](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/datawarehousing/sqlserver-airflow/08-performance): Measured on the Linux + Docker lab: rowstore vs nonclustered columnstore vs a pre-join indexed view vs an aggregated indexed view on SQL Server 2022 for Linux, and columnstore delta stores and their maintenance.
  - [Workload Management](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/datawarehousing/sqlserver-airflow/09-workload-management): Resource Governor on SQL Server 2022 for Linux: a classifier function puts the ETL login DataLoader into its own workload group and resource pool, the SQL Server equivalent of the course's Synapse workload classifier.
  - [The Data Quality Gate](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/datawarehousing/sqlserver-airflow/10-data-quality): A data quality gate on SQL Server 2022 for Linux: five rules, including reconciliation with the live source system, that fail the Airflow run and stop bad data from being published.
  - [Orchestration with Airflow](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/datawarehousing/sqlserver-airflow/11-orchestration-airflow): The sbecoltddw_e2e_pipeline DAG task by task: one SQL file per task, task groups, a file-driven deploy group, trigger rules, params, and the small operator that runs SQL files and surfaces every error.
  - [Running, Failing & Re-running](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/datawarehousing/sqlserver-airflow/12-run-fail-rerun): Real runs of the SBEcoLTDDW pipeline on Linux + Docker: a genuine failure from the first build fixed by clearing tasks, then an initial load, a no-change run, an SCD2 change, a failed data quality gate, the fix and a full reload.
  - [Serving the Data](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/datawarehousing/sqlserver-airflow/13-serving): The rpt reporting views of SBEcoLTDDW, as-was vs as-is reporting with an SCD2 dimension, access control for consumers, and what not to query.
  - [Script Index & Gotchas](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/datawarehousing/sqlserver-airflow/appendix-a-scripts): Every file of the SBEcoLTDDW lab with what it does, how to rebuild the lab, and the SQL Server 2022 on Linux and Airflow surprises hit while building it.

## Proactive Database Administration

- [Proactive Database Administration track](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dba/): The Proactive Database Administration track: health checks, baselines and alerts that find problems in SQL Server and Amazon Redshift before users do.
- [Proactive DBA](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dba/proactive-dba/): Proactive database administration for SQL Server and Amazon Redshift: daily health checks, baselines, thresholds and alerts that catch problems before users notice.
  - [Proactive SQL Server Administration](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dba/proactive-dba/01-sql-server): A daily SQL Server health check: backup age, CHECKDB and corruption alerts, disk and log space, VLFs, wait-statistics baselines, Query Store regressions, blocking, stale statistics, security drift, failed jobs, index defragmentation and reclaiming space.
  - [Proactive Amazon Redshift Administration](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dba/proactive-dba/02-redshift): A daily Amazon Redshift health check: table skew, unsorted rows and stale statistics, vacuum and analyze, query queueing, WLM query monitoring rules, disk spills, long transactions, load errors, Advisor recommendations, re-sorting with VACUUM and deep copy, and reclaiming storage.

## dbt, from engine to metaprogramming

- [dbt, from engine to metaprogramming track](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/): The dbt track: dbt Core architecture and internals, followed by advanced dbt Jinja and metaprogramming.
- [dbt Core Architecture & Internals](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/core-architecture/): How dbt Core works inside: packages, configuration loading, the parser and manifest, the DAG, the Jinja compiler, the execution engine and artifacts.
  - [The Big Picture](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/core-architecture/01-big-picture): What dbt Core is, its compiler/scheduler/executor architecture, how it compares with dbt Fusion and the dbt platform, and what happens step by step during a dbt run.
  - [Package Anatomy](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/core-architecture/02-package-anatomy): The Python distributions behind dbt Core — dbt-core, dbt-common, dbt-adapters, dbt-postgres, dbt-extractor — and the modules inside each one.
  - [CLI & Configuration Loading](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/core-architecture/03-cli-and-config): How dbt's Click CLI, flags, dbtRunner, profiles.yml, dbt_project.yml, vars and env vars are resolved into a RuntimeConfig.
  - [The Parser & the Manifest](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/core-architecture/04-parser-and-manifest): How dbt turns project files into the manifest: node types, parse order, the static parser, config precedence, partial parsing and manifest.json.
  - [The DAG & Node Selection](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/core-architecture/05-dag-and-selection): How dbt builds its DAG with networkx, how the selector engine resolves --select, --exclude and YAML selectors, indirect test selection, and how GraphQueue feeds worker threads.
  - [Compilation & the Jinja Engine](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/core-architecture/06-compilation-and-jinja): dbt's sandboxed Jinja environment, its custom extensions, how the render context is assembled in layers, macro resolution order, ephemeral CTE injection and compiled vs run output.
  - [The Execution Engine](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/core-architecture/07-execution-engine): Tasks and runners, the thread pool, the relation cache, connections and transactions, and a line-by-line walk through the incremental materialization that builds dimemployee.
  - [Artifacts & State](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/core-architecture/08-artifacts-and-state): dbt's artifacts — manifest, run_results, catalog, sources — their schemas, state comparison, deferral, dbt retry, and patterns for orchestrating dbt with Airflow.
- [Advanced dbt Jinja](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/): Advanced dbt Jinja: the rendering model, macros, compile-time queries, dispatch, overriding internals, custom materializations, tests and the graph object.
  - [How dbt Renders Jinja](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/01-rendering-model): The rendering model behind dbt Jinja: where Jinja runs, parse versus execute, output versus return values, and how to see exactly what a template produced.
  - [Syntax Deep Dive](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/02-syntax-deep-dive): Jinja delimiters, whitespace control, literals, operators, filters, tests, loops and raw blocks, with the details that matter when the output is SQL.
  - [Data Types & Scope](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/03-types-and-scope): Jinja values are Python objects: lists, dicts, namespace(), do, block set, loop scoping, macro scope, truthiness and type conversion in dbt.
  - [Built-in Context Objects](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/04-context-objects): A guided tour of dbt's Jinja context: this, target, model, config, adapter, var, env_var, modules, flags, invocation_id, run_started_at, exceptions, builtins and more.
  - [ref, source & config Internals](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/05-ref-source-config): What ref(), source() and config() really do at parse and run time, Relation objects in depth, config merging rules, and is_incremental() traced through dimemployee.
  - [Writing Macros](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/06-writing-macros): dbt macros in depth: arguments, defaults, varargs and kwargs, return(), caller() and call blocks, recursion, namespacing, documenting macros and argument validation.
  - [Compile-time Queries](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/07-compile-time-queries): run_query, statement blocks and load_result, working with agate tables, the execute guard, and building a dynamic pivot from live data.
  - [Dynamic SQL Generation](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/08-dynamic-sql): Generating SQL from metadata: column lists from YAML and introspection, robust row hashes for SCD2, CASE from mappings, unions, cross-database macros, escaping and quoting.
  - [Hooks & Operations](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/09-hooks-and-operations): pre_hook and post_hook rendering and transactions, on-run-start and on-run-end with the results object, run-operation, and a deep dive into the record_dim_stats hook.
  - [Dispatch & Adapter Macros](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/10-dispatch): adapter.dispatch in depth: implementation naming, adapter inheritance, macro_namespace, search_order overrides in dbt_project.yml, and overriding dbt's built-in and package macros.
  - [Overriding dbt Internals](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/11-overriding-internals): generate_schema_name, generate_alias_name and generate_database_name, environment-aware naming, overriding ref with builtins, and overriding built-in tests.
  - [Custom Materializations](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/12-custom-materializations): Anatomy of a dbt materialization and a step-by-step build of an scd2 materialization for PostgreSQL: relations, hooks, statements, transactions and returning relations.
  - [Custom Generic Tests](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/13-custom-tests): Writing generic tests with {% test %} blocks: arguments, implicit model and column_name, configs like severity, where, error_if and store_failures, plus a reusable SCD2 integrity test.
  - [The graph Object](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/14-graph-object): Walking graph.nodes and graph.sources from Jinja: project-wide checks, grants, lineage walks, YAML-driven SQL and selected_resources.
  - [Debugging Jinja](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/15-debugging): A systematic way to debug dbt Jinja: locate the phase, inspect compiled output, log values, use --debug logs, raise clear errors, and decode common error messages.
  - [Packages](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/16-packages): Installing and pinning dbt packages, what dbt_utils, dbt_expectations and codegen offer, reading package source, and building your own internal macro package.
  - [Anti-patterns & Performance](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/17-anti-patterns): When Jinja hurts: over-templating, hidden dependencies, parse-time cost, compile-time queries, hard-coded locations, silent defaults, and a review checklist.
  - [Capstone: a Metadata-driven Dimension Loader](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/18-capstone): Capstone: turn dimemployee into a metadata-driven SCD2 dimension generated from config meta, with validated inputs, generated SQL, generic hooks, an integrity test, a graph-based audit operation and a safe rollout.
  - [Context Cheat Sheet](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/appendix-a-cheat-sheet): Every commonly used dbt Jinja context member on one page, with where it is available and a one-line example.
  - [Filter Reference](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/appendix-b-filters): The Jinja filters and tests that matter in dbt, grouped by task, with SQL-generation examples, plus dbt's own filters.
  - [Glossary](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/dbt/jinja-advanced/appendix-c-glossary): Definitions of the terms used across the dbt Core internals and Advanced dbt Jinja tutorials.

## Power Electronics

- [Power Electronics track](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/power-electronics/): The Power Electronics track: converters, inverters and control for solar, wind and battery storage systems.
- [Power Electronics for Renewable Energy](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/power-electronics/renewable-energy/): Power Electronics for Renewable Energy: converters, MPPT, inverters, grid connection, wind conversion and battery storage, explained from first principles.
  - [The Big Picture](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/power-electronics/renewable-energy/01-big-picture): Why solar, wind and battery systems all depend on power electronics, the four kinds of power conversion, why converters switch instead of dissipating, and how efficiency adds up across a conversion chain.
  - [Semiconductor Switches](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/power-electronics/renewable-energy/02-semiconductor-switches): The switches inside every converter: diodes, MOSFETs, IGBTs and the wide-bandgap devices silicon carbide and gallium nitride. How they conduct, how they lose power, and how to choose one from its datasheet.
  - [Switching, PWM & Losses](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/power-electronics/renewable-energy/03-switching-and-losses): Pulse-width modulation and duty cycle, what happens inside a hard switching transition, every loss mechanism in a power switch, the switching-frequency trade-off, dead time and thermal design.
  - [DC-DC Converters](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/power-electronics/renewable-energy/04-dc-dc-converters): The buck, boost and buck-boost converters derived from volt-second balance: conversion ratios, inductor and capacitor ripple, continuous and discontinuous conduction, non-ideal boost gain and a complete PV boost design.
  - [Maximum Power Point Tracking](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/power-electronics/renewable-energy/05-mppt): How a PV converter finds and holds the maximum power point: the PV curve and how sun and temperature move it, perturb-and-observe and incremental conductance, partial shading and global scans, and the sensing electronics behind them.
  - [Inverters](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/power-electronics/renewable-energy/06-inverters): Turning DC into grid AC: half-bridge, H-bridge and three-phase bridges, bipolar and unipolar sinusoidal PWM, space-vector PWM, dead-time distortion, sizing the DC link for single-phase power pulsation, and grid-connected current control.
  - [Isolated DC-DC Converters](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/power-electronics/renewable-energy/07-isolated-converters): When and how to isolate a DC-DC converter: transformer basics and core reset, the flyback, forward and phase-shifted full-bridge converters, the LLC resonant converter with a 400 V to 48 V battery design, and the dual active bridge.
  - [Gate Drivers & Isolation](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/power-electronics/renewable-energy/08-gate-drivers): Driving MOSFETs, IGBTs, SiC and GaN switches: gate charge and peak current, choosing gate resistors, drive voltages, Miller-induced turn-on and negative bias, bootstrap and isolated high-side drivers, CMTI, desaturation protection and gate-loop layout.
  - [Magnetics: Inductors & Transformers](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/power-electronics/renewable-energy/09-magnetics): Designing the magnetic components of a converter: Faraday's and Ampère's laws, air gaps and saturation, ferrite, powder and nanocrystalline cores, core and winding losses, skin effect, the area-product method, a complete PV boost inductor design and an LLC transformer.
  - [Filters, EMI & PCB Layout](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/power-electronics/renewable-energy/10-filters-emi-layout): Keeping a fast converter clean and quiet: the LCL grid filter with a worked 3 kW design and damping, grid harmonic limits, leakage current in transformerless PV inverters, conducted EMI and its differential- and common-mode paths, EMI filters, and the PCB layout rules for the power loop, gate loop and switch node.
  - [Control & Simulation](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/power-electronics/renewable-energy/11-control-simulation): Closing the loops of a renewable converter: averaged models, the boost converter's transfer function and right-half-plane zero, voltage-mode and current-mode control, designing cascaded PI loops, slope compensation, digital delay, the control structure of a PV inverter, and simulating the boost converter in Python.
  - [Thermal Design, Reliability & Protection](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/power-electronics/renewable-energy/12-thermal-reliability-protection): Making a converter last twenty years outdoors: the loss budget and a shared heatsink, transient thermal impedance and thermal cycling, power-cycling lifetime, electrolytic and film capacitor lifetime, cosmic-ray derating, and the protection functions every PV inverter needs: overcurrent, overvoltage, surge, insulation and residual-current monitoring, and anti-islanding.
  - [Formula Sheet](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/power-electronics/renewable-energy/appendix-a-formulas): Every converter equation from the Power Electronics for Renewable Energy tutorial on one page: switches, losses, DC-DC converters, MPPT, inverters, isolated converters, gate drive, magnetics, filters, control and thermal design.

## Snowflake

- [Snowflake track](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/snowflake/): The Snowflake track: a complete data platform on Snowflake, loaded from SQL Server, transformed with dbt and orchestrated by Airflow.
- [Snowflake Data Platform with dbt and Airflow](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/snowflake/wwi-dbt-airflow/): WideWorldImporters from SQL Server into Snowflake: Bronze, Silver, Gold and a Sales data mart built with dbt, tested, reconciled and orchestrated by Airflow.
  - [The Complete Design](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/snowflake/wwi-dbt-airflow/00-the-design): The five design diagrams of the WideWorldImporters Snowflake platform at full size: infrastructure, medallion architecture, the source OLTP model, the Gold model and the Sales data mart.
  - [The Big Picture](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/snowflake/wwi-dbt-airflow/01-big-picture): What the WideWorldImporters Snowflake platform does, the medallion approach, the rules it follows and how one invoice line travels from SQL Server to a report.
  - [The Lab](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/snowflake/wwi-dbt-airflow/02-the-lab): The lab: an Ubuntu VM deployed in AWS running SQL Server and Airflow in Docker, Airflow extended with dbt-snowflake, the project folders and the service user's key pair.
  - [The Source System](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/snowflake/wwi-dbt-airflow/03-source-system): WideWorldImporters on SQL Server 2022: four schemas, 31 tables, temporal tables and change columns, a read-only extract login, and the row-level security policy that hid every customer.
  - [Setting Up Snowflake](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/snowflake/wwi-dbt-airflow/04-snowflake-setup): One setup script: three warehouses, two databases, a stage and file format, three roles, a key-pair service user and a credit monitor.
  - [Extract & Load into Bronze](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/snowflake/wwi-dbt-airflow/05-extract-load-bronze): extract_load.py: high-water marks, gzipped CSV files, PUT to an internal stage, COPY INTO the Bronze tables and a load audit, with the real first load of 1,057,452 rows.
  - [The dbt Project](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/snowflake/wwi-dbt-airflow/06-dbt-project): The dbt project: folders as medallion layers, a key-pair profile with no secrets, exact schema names and generated staging models.
  - [Silver: Staging, Snapshots & Intermediate](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/snowflake/wwi-dbt-airflow/07-silver): The Silver layer: 31 generated staging views that keep the latest row per key with real types, five SCD Type 2 snapshots, and four intermediate models.
  - [Gold: Conformed Dimensions](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/snowflake/wwi-dbt-airflow/08-gold-dimensions): Eight conformed dimensions: hash surrogate keys, SCD Type 2 versions from snapshots, the first-version rule, the unknown member and a fiscal calendar that starts in November.
  - [Gold: Facts](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/snowflake/wwi-dbt-airflow/09-gold-facts): Six fact tables: point-in-time lookups of SCD2 dimension keys, the business rules behind every total, and incremental merges by load batch.
  - [The Sales Data Mart](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/snowflake/wwi-dbt-airflow/10-sales-data-mart): MART_SALES: one fact at invoice-line grain and six dimensions, role-playing keys, and real answers to the business questions it was designed for.
  - [Tests & Reconciliation](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/snowflake/wwi-dbt-airflow/11-tests-reconciliation): 123 dbt tests on keys and relationships, cautious test selection per layer, and a reconciliation that proves Snowflake matches the source system to the cent.
  - [Orchestration with Airflow](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/snowflake/wwi-dbt-airflow/12-airflow-dag): One DAG, ten BashOperator tasks, each a single shell command: the code, the task order and a real scheduled run.
  - [Commands & File Index](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/snowflake/wwi-dbt-airflow/appendix-a-commands): Every file in the WWI Snowflake project and every command to rebuild or re-run any step by hand.

## Statistics, taught with oil & energy data

- [Statistics, taught with oil & energy data track](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/statistics/): The Statistics track: practical statistics for everyday work, taught entirely with real open oil and energy datasets.
- [Statistics for Daily Use](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/statistics/zero-to-hero/): A fast, visual statistics course from first principles to advanced methods, built on real open oil and energy datasets with SQL and Python.
  - [Statistics in One Picture](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/statistics/zero-to-hero/01-big-picture): The whole of statistics on one map: population and sample, parameter and statistic, descriptive and inferential statistics, sampling designs and experiments — taught with world energy data and Norwegian exploration wells.
  - [Seeing Data](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/statistics/zero-to-hero/02-seeing-data): Variable types, frequency distributions, histograms, distribution shapes, mean, median, trimmed mean, standard deviation, quartiles, boxplots, z-scores, Chebyshev and the empirical rule — using oil fields, Brent prices and country energy data.
  - [The Probability Toolkit](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/statistics/zero-to-hero/03-probability): Probability for practitioners: events, Venn diagrams, addition and complement rules, contingency tables, conditional probability, independence, Bayes' rule and counting — using 1,380 Norwegian wildcat wells.
  - [Random Variables & Distributions](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/statistics/zero-to-hero/04-distributions): Discrete random variables, expected value, binomial and Poisson distributions, density curves, the normal distribution, normal probability plots and the normal approximation — with exploration campaigns, discovery counts and Brent returns.
  - [Sampling Distributions & the CLT](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/statistics/zero-to-hero/05-sampling-clt): Sampling error, the sampling distribution of the sample mean, standard error and the central limit theorem — simulated live on the real, extremely skewed population of Norwegian oil and gas field sizes.
  - [Confidence Intervals](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/statistics/zero-to-hero/06-confidence-intervals): Point estimates and confidence intervals: z and t intervals for a mean, margin of error, sample size, Student's t, intervals for a proportion (including plus-four) and for a standard deviation — on drilling times, discovery rates and oil-price volatility.
  - [The Hypothesis-Testing Engine](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/statistics/zero-to-hero/07-hypothesis-testing): Hypothesis testing end to end: null and alternative hypotheses, test statistics, critical values and p-values, Type I and II errors, power, z- and t-tests, the Wilcoxon signed-rank test and one-proportion tests — on U.S. crude inventories and Norwegian discovery rates.
  - [Comparing Two Groups](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/statistics/zero-to-hero/08-two-groups): Two-sample inference: pooled and Welch t-tests, paired t-test and paired Wilcoxon, Mann–Whitney, the F-test for two standard deviations and the two-proportion z-test — on refinery seasons, the Brent–WTI spread, oil volatility and exploration success.
  - [Categorical Data & Chi-Square](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/statistics/zero-to-hero/09-chi-square): Chi-square procedures for categorical data: the chi-square distribution, goodness-of-fit, contingency tables, conditional distributions, independence and homogeneity tests, standardised residuals and Cramér's V — on what Norwegian wildcats find, where and when.
  - [Regression & Correlation](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/statistics/zero-to-hero/10-regression): Simple linear regression and correlation end to end: least squares, slope interpretation, sums of squares and R², correlation, regression assumptions, slope inference, confidence vs prediction intervals and residual analysis — from Brent crude to U.S. pump prices.
  - [Analysis of Variance (ANOVA)](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/statistics/zero-to-hero/11-anova): One-way ANOVA explained visually: between- and within-group variation, sums of squares, the F-statistic and ANOVA table, assumptions and the rule of 2, Tukey multiple comparisons and the Kruskal–Wallis test — on water depth and drilling time across Norway's three sea areas.
  - [Hero Level: Real-World Methods](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/statistics/zero-to-hero/12-hero-level): Methods practitioners rely on: the bootstrap, permutation tests, multiple-testing corrections, autocorrelation and effective sample size, multiple regression and omitted-variable bias, decline curves, logistic regression and Bayesian updating — all on real oil and gas data.
  - [Data, Code & Reproducibility](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/statistics/zero-to-hero/data-sources): The open energy datasets behind the Statistics course, their licences, the PostgreSQL schema, the analysis pipeline and how to reproduce every number.
  - [Formula Sheet](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/statistics/zero-to-hero/formula-sheet): Every formula of the Statistics for Daily Use course on one printable page — descriptive measures, probability, distributions, intervals, tests, chi-square, regression and ANOVA.
  - [Which Test Do I Use?](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/statistics/zero-to-hero/test-chooser): An interactive decision tree that picks the right statistical procedure — intervals, tests, chi-square, regression, ANOVA, bootstrap — with conditions, chapter links and Python one-liners.

## uv: Python Projects and Packaging

- [uv: Python Projects and Packaging track](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/uv/): The uv track: a hands-on tutorial on uv, the fast Python package and project manager, from first install to workspaces, Docker images and CI/CD pipelines.
- [uv Hands-On: From First Script to Production](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/uv/hands-on/): A hands-on uv tutorial from beginner to advanced: installing uv, Python versions, scripts, projects, dependencies, lockfiles, tools, the pip interface, workspaces, Docker, CI/CD and internals.
  - [Why uv](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/uv/hands-on/01-why-uv): What problem uv solves, which tools it replaces (pip, pip-tools, virtualenv, pyenv, pipx, Poetry), why it is fast, and the three-file mental model used throughout the uv tutorial.
  - [Installing uv and First Commands](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/uv/hands-on/02-install): Install uv on Windows, macOS and Linux with the standalone installer, WinGet, Homebrew or pip; check the install, update uv, enable shell completion and run your first commands.
  - [Managing Python Versions](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/uv/hands-on/03-python-versions): Install, list, find, pin and remove Python versions with uv python, use .python-version files and the --python option, and understand how uv chooses an interpreter.
  - [Scripts with Inline Dependencies](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/uv/hands-on/04-scripts): Run single-file Python scripts with uv run, add dependencies with --with or inline script metadata (PEP 723), make scripts executable with a uv shebang, and lock script dependencies.
  - [Your First Project](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/uv/hands-on/05-projects): Create a uv project with uv init, understand pyproject.toml, add dependencies with uv add, run code with uv run, package a command-line app with a src layout, and use the .venv in your editor.
  - [Dependencies in Depth](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/uv/hands-on/06-dependencies): Version specifiers and markers, development dependency groups, optional extras, git, path and editable sources, private and alternative package indexes, and upgrading dependencies safely with uv.
  - [The Lockfile and Sync](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/uv/hands-on/07-lockfile-sync): What uv.lock contains, universal cross-platform resolution, uv lock and uv sync, exact syncing, the --locked and --frozen options, resolution strategies, exclude-newer and exporting to requirements.txt or pylock.toml.
  - [Command-Line Tools with uvx](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/uv/hands-on/08-tools): Run Python command-line tools with uvx without installing them, pin tool versions, install tools permanently with uv tool install, upgrade and remove them, and decide between a tool and a dev dependency.
  - [The pip Interface and Migration](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/uv/hands-on/09-pip-interface): Use uv venv and uv pip as fast drop-in replacements for venv, pip and pip-tools, compile and sync requirements files, and migrate requirements.txt and Poetry projects to uv projects.
  - [Workspaces, Building and Publishing](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/uv/hands-on/10-workspaces-packaging): Organise several Python packages in one repository with a uv workspace and a single lockfile, choose a build backend, version with uv version, build wheels with uv build and publish to PyPI with uv publish and trusted publishing.
  - [uv in Docker and CI/CD](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/uv/hands-on/11-docker-ci): Build small, cache-friendly Docker images with uv using multi-stage builds, cache mounts and layer ordering, and run fast, reproducible GitHub Actions pipelines with setup-uv, test matrices and trusted publishing.
  - [Internals, Configuration and Troubleshooting](https://engineeringwithbandarage.github.io/uv/hands-on/12-internals): How uv's global cache and link modes work, how the PubGrub resolver and forking resolution find versions, where uv reads configuration and environment variables, and how to fix the most common uv errors.
